Simpler Windows setup: unzip, open TenchuZ.exe, and choose your own disc image.

- Windows now includes portable Python and the compiler. No separate Python, Visual Studio, Clang, or Windows SDK installation is needed.
- First-start preparation works offline without administrator access or PATH changes. It takes a few minutes and removes temporary compiler files when finished.
- Setup.cmd opens the game directly. Incomplete packages report that the full ZIP needs to be extracted, instead of asking players to install developer tools.
- Added a release check that builds and loads a test DLL with system Python and compiler paths removed.
- Includes all v0.3.3 fixes for loading-related movement slowdown, loading/dialog textures, portable saves, language selection, and Linux version/updater detection.

Tested locally: full disc preparation with Windows-only PATH and empty compiler environment, village movement, mission loading, and the existing regression suite. The Windows download is larger because it now carries its own setup tools. Keep the included tools folder for future game-code updates.

Both packages are built from this tag and checked for the correct version before publication. The Linux package targets glibc 2.35 for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer, including SteamOS.

Updating: use the in-game updater, or close the game and extract the package over your existing installation, preserving your saves and settings. Linux users whose older release reports "dev" should install this update manually once. Third-party launchers may still show an outdated prerequisite checklist; open TenchuZ.exe directly.

Known reports still under investigation: overbright training floors on some AMD GPUs and a reported mission-start crash. This release does not claim to fix those reports.
